applies_why: This judge text decides whether verses pressed against C3 count as unanswered witnesses for a broken link, which is the subject of K-G4.
quote: JUDGE STATEMENT: the line is cured by retraction, not defended: every witness pressed against C3 was named and answered in the challenger's own later rounds ((DR2) §C and (DR3) C3 quoting Matthew 1:18, 1:25 and Deuteronomy 22:24; (DR3) C4 quoting Luke 1:34), so the "witness left unanswered" ground fails and the collision is regraded UNDERDETERMINED
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.
room: The room is 'A verse the judge says was answered is not counted': I weighed reading that an answered verse may be dropped without quoting the earlier pressing sentence against reading that the pressing-quote condition must first be satisfied; the answered-verse exception controls here.
why: Because K-G4 expressly says an answered verse is not counted, the judge's retraction of the witnesses does not count them toward a broken link and therefore does not breach the rule.
